newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium takes to streets over child sex scandal.
newsitem.headline: Belgium takes to streets over child sex scandal.

text.p: Belgians began streaming into Brussels early on Sunday to demonstrate their disgust with an official system that allowed a paedophile ring to operate and to express their sympathy with its victims.
Police unofficially estimated that more than 100,000 people would take part in the mass demonstration and one newspaper said that Belgium was sitting astride a volcano.

Interior Minister Johan Vande Lanotte has said the government could fall unless it satisfies the public over its inquiries into the sexual abuse and murder of four girls -- two of whom were starved to death -- and the sexual abuse of at least two others.

With appeals for calm and dignity ringing in their ears, the demonstrators, wearing white and carrying white flowers as a symbol of support and hope, planned to march through the country's capital from the Gare du Nord to the Gare du Midi.

The White March follows a week of protests that broke out spontaneously after Belgium's top court removed a popular magistrate from investigations into the paedophile ring alleged to have been led by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux.

The Cour de Cassation ruled that magistrate Jean-Marc Connerotte had compromised himself by accepting a free dinner from the Marc et Corine group that specialises in helping the parents of missing children.
The ruling, following the letter rather than the spirit of the law, prompted an already morally-outraged public to take to the streets amid widespread allegations of a high-level cover-up.

The demonstrations became increasingly violent as tens of thousands of students took the opportunity to add their voices to the general clamour for a radical clean-up of a justice system seen as corrupt.

About 3,000 motorcyclists from all over the linguistically-divided nation rode through central Brussels, bringing traffic to a halt, on Saturday as part of the protests against alleged judicial bungling and corruption in the scandal.

In addition to demonstrating support for the parents of the missing and dead children, they demanded that sex offenders should not be paroled and, in some case, sought reinstatement of the death penalty.
Dutroux, one of 13 people so far charged in connection with the case, was released 10 years early in 1992 from a 13-year sentence for multiple child rape.
Belgium erased the death sentence from its statute books in June after it had lain largely neglected for most of this century.

The parents of the dead children -- Julie Lejeune, Melissa Russo, Eefje Lambrecks and An Marchal -- and those of two missing girls -- Elisabeth Brichet and Loubna Benaissa -- have specifically ruled out a return of the death penalty.
Belgian railways said on Friday it had already pre-sold 40,000 subsidised return tickets to the Brussels demonstration and expected the number to double.
Coaches have also been booked all over the country, while free parking and free bus and metro services will be provided in Brussels. The forecast is for fair weather.
